thread.title_full: Meeting planned on Oct. 26 for Hanover's Safe Streets for All project - NewsBreak

author: Harrison Jones
title: Meeting planned on Oct. 26 for Hanover's Safe Streets for All project - NewsBreak
text:
By Harrison Jones ,
15 hours ago A public meeting is planned amid the development of Hanover's Safe Streets for All action plan, with the public invited to give input on areas of concern.
Development of the plan consists of a 12-month study that launched in September, which Hanover officials said will combine research, traffic data, and the community's input to identify road safety issues as well as to develop strategies and projects to improve traffic safety across Hanover.
Once developed in 2027, the project will provide officials with an action plan of safety improvements and programs, along with the priority in which those actions should be completed.
A 'public engagement meeting' for the action plan is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, according to an announcement for the meeting.
The meeting will be held in the council chambers of the Hanover Borough Public Administration building, located at 33 Frederick Street in downtown Hanover.
Along with an introduction to the study, the public meeting will include a workshop with several interactive activities for participants, according to the agenda.
Public input will be accepted on area-wide issues of programs and policy; on the locations of problem areas and safety concerns; and regarding the times of day that are of greatest concern.
All three areas of public input during the activities will encourage participants to share their suggestions for potential solutions for issues, the meeting agenda states.
An interpreter will be available at the meeting to assist Spanish-speaking and Portuguese-speaking attendees, the release shared, and individuals requiring special accommodations are asked to notify the municipality in advance.
Survey ends Oct. 31 According to Hanover officials, the first public survey shared on the project's website is intended to be completed by Oct. 31, 2026, closing five days after the public meeting.
That survey can be answered online at the website, located at engage-dewberry.com/Hanover-SSAP , where members of the Hanover community can answer a brief survey regarding their traffic and pedestrian concerns.
The 19-question survey primarily focuses on the ways in which a respondent typically travels in Hanover, and the safety concerns that they typically see.
In one question, the survey asks respondents how effective various potential safety solutions could be around Hanover, including lower speed limits, more crosswalks, more traffic signals, the addition of roundabouts, speed humps, bike lanes, and more.
The survey is the first of two community surveys, according to the project website, with a project timeline showing a future "Winter 2026 Survey" later in the timeline.
Over 230 pins dropped On a mapping tool provided on the project website, users can place markers on a map of Hanover to report near-miss incidents, suggest improvements, report a safety concern, or leave a comment on a location.
As of Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, the mapping tool listed 236 contributions.
Among those contributions, clusters of concerns or suggestions drew attention to problem intersections in the Hanover area.
The areas with the highest number of markers left by users, as of Oct. 21, consisted of 14 markers at the intersection of Ridge and Moul Avenue; 12 comments for Center Square; 10 for the intersection of Grant Drive and Moul Avenue; 9 for the intersection of Broadway and Wilson Avenue; and a tie of 7 comments at both the intersection of Third Street and High Street along with seven at the intersection of Broadway and Eisenhower Drive.
In what was so far the most comments of anywhere in Hanover, 14 comments were left in the area where Moul Avenue meets Middle Street and Ridge Avenue.
The intersection has seen numerous crashes over the years, including numerous tractor-trailers that use Ridge Avenue to access industrial areas on the northeast side of Hanover.
Many of the comments noted the poor visibility available for drivers coming towards the intersection in all directions, with several comments suggesting a four-way stop and two suggesting a traffic signal for the intersection.
Twelve notes were left in the Center Square of Hanover, mainly voicing concerns over pedestrian and bicyclist safety at the square, along issues for vehicles and pedestrians with signal timing and the doubled-up traffic signals.
The intersection in Center Square, along with the nearby intersection of York Street and Broadway, will be the subject of an upcoming safety improvement project, which will retime the signals and remove the doubled-up traffic signals and crosswalks in the square.
If you go: What: Hanover Safe Streets for All Public Engagement Meeting Where: Council Chambers inside the Hanover Public Administration Building, 33 Frederick Street, Hanover When: 6:30 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 More information: engage-dewberry.com/Hanover-SSAP Harrison Jones is the Hanover reporter for The Evening Sun. Contact him at hjones@usatodayco.com .
